title: Spell Formula 1: print()
lessonSummary: Your first spell works! With print() you can put anything on the screen.

tasks.instruction: Run this example and look at the output below.
tasks.codeTemplate:
print("Hello, world!")
print("Welcome to Pyralia!")

# An empty line makes things easier to read
print()
print("=== Your program is running! ===")

tasks.instruction: Use print() to output your own welcome message that contains the word "adventure".

title: Spell Formula 2: Variables
lessonSummary: Perfect! Variables let you keep values and change them later.

tasks.instruction: Run this example. It shows text and number variables.
tasks.codeTemplate:
hero_name = "Aria"   # Text (String)
hero_level = 1       # Number (Integer)

print(hero_name)
print(hero_level)

tasks.instruction: Store the text "Elvenwood" in a variable called place and print the variable with print().
Create a variable gold with the value 50. Then change it to 150 and print gold.

title: Spell Formula 3: Joining Texts
lessonSummary: Exactly how you build whole sentences from texts and numbers – don't forget str() for numbers!

tasks.instruction: Run this example – notice where str() is needed.
tasks.codeTemplate:
name = "Legolas"
weapon = "Bow"
arrows = 20

print("Hero: " + name)
print("Arrows: " + str(arrows))
print(name + " fights with " + weapon + " and has " + str(arrows) + " arrows.")

validation.expected: Legolas fights with Bow and has 20 arrows.

tasks.instruction: Create a variable arrows with the value 20 and use + and str() to print exactly this text: Arrows: 20

title: Spell Formula 4: input()
lessonSummary: Now your program can talk to people – input() makes it interactive.

tasks.instruction: Run this example. An input window opens – enter a name there.
tasks.codeTemplate:
name = input("What is your hero's name? ")
print("Welcome, " + name + "!")

tasks.instruction: Use input() to ask for your hero's weapon, store the answer in weapon and print: Battle-ready with: (followed by the weapon) (When checking, Warhammer is entered automatically.)

title: Spell Formula 5: Comments
lessonSummary: Comments are your secret notes – Python ignores them, but they help you find your way around your code.

tasks.instruction: Run this example. Notice which line is NOT executed.
tasks.codeTemplate:
# This line prints the hero's name
print("Aragorn")

print("Level 5")  # shows the current level

print("This will run")
# print("This will NOT run")

tasks.instruction: Write a comment of your own, followed by a print() that outputs exactly: Comment read
